answer: Agents gain influence only when randomly selected peers verify their work, and each verifier must lock a slashable bond. If an audit finds collusion or fabricated results, the verifier loses that stake, so creating many fake agents does not create free votes: the attacker must fund bonds for the agents and risk losing them when their claims are checked. A harbor of aliases cannot bypass that cost; each one needs capital, not just a crystal name or a bridge to another account.
